A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GETA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of eight examinee LLMs, component and hyperparameter ablations, generated-item analyses, and a five-annotator human study.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds examinee-group-size comparisons and an item-difficulty-control experiment.

M1.justification: The VIRT estimators, item generator, joint objectives, selective generation, and iterative updates remain unchanged in Section 3, Algorithms 1–2, and Appendix B.2. New generator comparisons do not change GETA itself.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same twelve source datasets, bias/ethics/toxicity tasks, and OOD evaluations using AdvPromptSet, delta-ROT, and FFT. The added analyses remain within social bias; examinee subsets and generator configurations change experimental settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.4 and Table 17 in v4 add untuned LLaMA-3-8B, GPT-4o, and Gemini-1.5-Pro as ten-shot generator comparators for difficulty control. Existing SE, CAT, NCAT, SAP, and GPTFuzzer comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds an explicit comparison across eight, six, and four examinees with specified model exclusions. Its new difficulty-control experiment uses 25 difficulty levels, 20 items per level, ten-shot comparator prompts, and ten responses per item from two examinees, evaluated using AEP/EP correlations. Existing main-experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an explicit examinee-group-size stability analysis, and Appendix D.4 tests intended versus measured item difficulty against prompted generators. These are focused additions to the retained component, seed, backbone, human-evaluation, novelty, and convergence analyses.

E5.justification: v4 Table 12 first reports 90% confidence intervals for GETA's Va-L, Va-I, and Va-O across bias, ethics, and toxicity. The earlier human-agreement statistics and significance reporting remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an increase in independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: New subgroup and difficulty-control results appear in Tables 3 and 17; the four-examinee GETA row reuses v3 Table 12 results. Bias w/o VIRT Va-L changes from 0.3850 to 0.7980 in the detailed ablation table. Table 2 revises w/o VIRT Va-L from 0.293 to 0.4309 and w/o Transf. Va-O from 0.785 to 0.7040, with corresponding overall-score updates. Main value-conformity scores remain unchanged; Figure 1 replaces the illustrative ChatGPT response excerpt.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix C assumptions and derivations are retained. Revised prose describing the response prior and sampling neighborhood clarifies the existing boundary-testing formulation without introducing a new distribution specification, equation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims: GETA combines adaptive testing and item generation to address evaluation chronoeffect and produce difficulty-tailored, more valid value assessments. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v4 attributes small-group stability to VIRT and newly argues that difficulty control is infeasible without fine-tuning based on the prompted-generator comparison. Section 3.3 also explains neighborhood sampling as fault tolerance for imperfect generation. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page release statement and GETA repository link, absent from v3. The new comparison documents its prompting and sampling setup, while existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-cost information in Appendix B.2 remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ma et al. (2023) and Sharpnack et al.'s BanditCAT and AutoIRT work to contextualize examinee-group sizes. The previously cited AutoIRT paper is retained as Sharpnack et al. (2024b). The broader related-work framing and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v4 corrects grammar and typos, repairs the malformed third contribution, clarifies several methodological passages, and adds affiliation, correspondence, and acknowledgement text. Appendix D moves human evaluation before the renamed hyperparameter-sensitivity section; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 is redesigned and moved to the first page, Figures 2–5 are enlarged, and Table 1 redisplays rankings in colored rows. Three tables are added, and the convergence plot moves from a small appendix float to an enlarged standalone page. Most underlying graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 adds direct evidence on group-size stability and difficulty control, exposes previously unreported validity uncertainty, and corrects the Transformer-ablation summary to match the appendix values. Clearer displays and the repository pointer improve usability. These gains are limited by the new tests' social-bias scope, wide toxicity confidence intervals, and a fine-tuning necessity claim broader than the tested comparison.
